Meetra Surik — article extraction

Source requested: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Meetra_Surik
Final URL: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Meetra_Surik (no redirect)
Page sections reviewed: The Mandalorian Wars; The Dark Wars; The Dark Wars > In search of the Lost Jedi; The Dark Wars > Against the Sith Triumvirate; Personality and traits > Darth Sion; Powers and abilities; Notes and references.

Scope note
- This is an extraction of what the article states, not an independent canon judgment.
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- “Feat” below means an action or outcome the article narrates. “Statement/opinion” marks dialogue, assessment, hype, or a character’s interpretation.
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- The article labels itself as a Legends article and warns that parts are no longer up to date.
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)

WOUND IN THE FORCE / MALACHOR V
Section: The Mandalorian Wars; reiterated in Powers and abilities.
- Surik commanded the final battle at Malachor V and ordered activation of the Mass Shadow Generator when Republic forces would not arrive in time. The generator crushed the Republic and Mandalorian forces caught in its wake. [8]
- The deaths and destruction at Malachor caused “such a substantial wound in the Force” that the shock would have killed Surik. The article says she unconsciously and instinctively severed her own connection to survive. [15]
- Afterward, she was deaf to the Force: the Force-echoes of the suffering she had caused and witnessed interfered with her ability to sense it. [15]
- The article states that she was the only Jedi under Revan who turned away from the dark side after Malachor V, and the only one who voluntarily returned to Coruscant to face trial and defend her actions. [8]
- The Council feared the “wound” surrounding her and considered the wound to have left her “dead.” Those are Council assessments, not independent feats. [8][17]
- On the rebuilt Dantooine Council, the Masters said she had become a wound in the Force, carried the deaths at Malachor, and regained her Force connection by feeding on death and leeching companions’ life energy. They claimed the Sith learned to feed on the Force from her and that she might reach Darth Nihilus’s magnitude and consume the galaxy; the article immediately says this “wasn’t true.” Treat this as an in-story Council theory, explicitly rejected by the article, not as a feat or valid scaling. [8]
- Kreia calls Surik “a dead spot in the Force” and says she sees in her the potential to see the Force die. This is Kreia’s statement/interpretation, not a demonstrated feat. [8]

CONCRETE FEATS AND POWER STATEMENTS
Section: Powers and abilities.
- The article says Surik naturally formed Force bonds with people around her, usually without conscious awareness. It says she unconsciously fed on deaths during her search for the Jedi Masters, fuelling her powers; this is the article’s description of her condition, not a quantified power level. [8][28]
- Vrook calls her “undisciplined” and “mediocre,” while Vandar calls her “an average student of the Force.” Kavar says she had a “deep” and “strong” connection as a Padawan, and Revan recalls her as “a powerful Jedi” with recognizable potential during the Mandalorian Wars. These are conflicting character assessments/statements, not feats. [9][27][2]
- Through Kreia’s instruction, she learned rare/advanced techniques including Breath control, Beast trick, and a powerful form of mind reading. The article says Kreia was impressed by how quickly she learned mind reading, noting most Masters studied it for years. This is a cited training/power statement. [8]
- The article lists Force valor, Force resistance, Force whirlwind, Force deflection, Force healing, Mind trick, Force Enlightenment, Force Channel, and other techniques learned from companions. [8]
- Surik defeated Azkul, Vaklu, Atris, Darth Sion, and Darth Nihilus, according to the article’s summary. The detailed accounts below qualify the Sion, Nihilus, and Traya encounters. [8]
- In hand-to-hand combat she defeated five of six Handmaiden sisters. On Dxun she defeated the Mandalorian battle-circle champions Kelborn and Bralor and became champion. [8]
- The article says she was one of the few Jedi able to use Dun Möch, especially in her duel with Sion, who “could not be defeated by normal means.” It says she used it to convince Sion to release his hatred, the Force, and his life. [8]
- As a war leader, she became Revan’s most trusted general, commanded over half of the Republic fleet, and took part in victorious battles at Dxun and Malachor V. [2][8]
- At Khoonda, she recruited civilians, healed injured militia, planted mines, repaired turrets and droids, and turned a disorganized defense into an army that defeated Azkul’s larger force within hours. [8]

VERSUS DARTH NIHILUS
Section: The Dark Wars > Against the Sith Triumvirate; also Powers and abilities.
- Nihilus sent his Shadow Hand, Visas Marr, to assassinate Surik. Surik defeated Marr in a brief lightsaber duel, redeemed her, and retrained her as a Jedi Sentinel. This is a direct Surik victory over Nihilus’s apprentice/agent, not a direct victory over Nihilus. [8]
- At the Battle of Telos IV, Surik confronted Nihilus aboard the Ravager to prevent him from destroying Telos to feed his hunger for the Force. She was assisted by Visas Marr and Mandalore the Preserver. [8]
- The article says Nihilus proved formidable and stunned Surik. Marr offered her life in exchange for Surik’s, distracting Nihilus long enough for Surik to recover. Marr then used her bond with Nihilus to weaken him; the team vanquished him. [8][21]
- Thus the article supports a team-assisted victory over Nihilus after he temporarily incapacitated Surik. It does not support an unassisted, clean solo victory. [8][21]

VERSUS DARTH SION
Sections: The Dark Wars > In search of the Lost Jedi; The Dark Wars > Against the Sith Triumvirate; Personality and traits > Darth Sion; Powers and abilities.
- At Korriban, Sion confronted Surik after killing Master Lonna Vash. Surik and her companions struck him down multiple times, but he recovered from fatal injuries and continued fighting. Kreia said Sion was not a normal creature of flesh and blood and that this was not a battle that could be won at that time; Surik fled. [8]
- At Malachor V, Surik fought through Sith Assassins, Lords, and Marauders, then confronted and defeated Sion multiple times. The article says she persuaded him to let go of his hatred and life and succumb to his injuries. [8]
- The article specifically ties this victory to Dun Möch, stating Sion could not be defeated by normal means. The decisive outcome is Surik’s combat plus persuasion, not a claim that ordinary damage alone killed him. [8]
- Sion says Surik is “beautiful” to him and that she is his weakness; his final words call her Kreia’s ultimate weakness as well. These are Sion’s statements about attachment/weakness, not objective power scaling. [8]

VERSUS DARTH TRAYA / KREIA
Sections: The Dark Wars > Against the Sith Triumvirate; Powers and abilities.
- After the reconvened Jedi Council tried to strip Surik of the Force, Kreia revealed herself as Darth Traya and drained the Masters of their powers. The article leaves Surik helpless/still in the Council’s stasis during this event; it is not a Surik feat. [8]
- After Kreia left, Surik defeated Atris, who had fallen to the dark side and was described by Kreia as having become a Darth Traya. Surik persuaded Atris to forgive her and helped her recognize the error of her beliefs. Atris then confirmed Kreia’s Sith identity and location. [8]
- On Malachor V, Surik confronted Kreia in the Trayus Academy after defeating Sion. In a fierce, short battle, Surik severed Kreia’s remaining hand and their Force bond in a single stroke. Surik initially refused to kill her. [8]
- Kreia animated three lightsabers through the Force, forcing Surik to strike her down. The article therefore describes a final victory over Traya after a separate Force-controlled-lightsaber phase, not an effortless one-shot. [8]
- Before dying, Kreia told Surik she was “greater than any she had ever trained.” This is Kreia’s statement/hype, not a neutral feat or numeric scaling. [8]

ARTICLE-STATED SCALING AND HOW TO READ IT
- The Council’s comparison of Surik’s possible future power to Darth Nihilus’s magnitude is explicitly followed by “which wasn’t true”; it is rejected in the article and should not be used as factual scaling. [8]
- Revan’s “powerful Jedi” assessment, Kavar’s “deep”/“strong” connection, Mandalore’s statement that even his greatest warriors were no match for her, and Kreia’s “greater than any she had ever trained” are character statements/opinions. [2][8][27]
- The article states that Surik was the only known light-sided Jedi to use Dun Möch to its greatest extent. This is an article-level comparative claim, but it is not a general numerical tier. [8]
- The article says Surik’s trained Jedi were essential to rebuilding the nearly annihilated Jedi Order, and that her actions on Dantooine, Onderon, and Telos helped stabilize the Republic for thousands of years. These are long-term consequences, not direct combat scaling. [8]
